1. Infectious keratitis / corneal ulcer — acute painful red eye after outdoor exposure with rapidly progressive vision loss to hand motions is classic; high risk for vision-threatening corneal infection.
2. Corneal foreign body with secondary infection/abrasion — history of mowing suggests possible particulate trauma leading to corneal epithelial defect and reduced vision.
3. Acute angle-closure glaucoma — can cause severe eye pain, redness and marked vision loss; needs urgent IOP check to exclude.
4. Scleritis (infectious or autoimmune) — severe, deep ocular pain with redness and decreased vision can present similarly; less likely than corneal causes but important to consider.
5. Endophthalmitis or severe anterior uveitis — less likely without recent intraocular procedure but can cause painful red eye and profound vision loss; consider if any history of eye surgery/injection.

Recommended immediate next steps (urgent): emergent slit‑lamp exam with fluorescein staining (look for corneal epithelial defect/infiltrate), measurement of intraocular pressure, pupillary exam (afferent pupillary defect), and corneal scraping for Gram stain/culture if an ulcer is present — treat presumptively for bacterial keratitis until cultures return.
